issue.title: postgresql.psycopg2 dialect should support empty connection string for libpq to use PG… env vars

labels.name: engine
labels.description: engines, connections, transactions, isolation levels, execution options

issue.body:
The `postgresql.psycopg2` dialect fails to connect if no connection parameters are specified in the connection URL, even though the official `libpq` Pg client library that underlies `psycopg2` is perfectly capable of [reading all connection parameters from `PG…` environment variables](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-envars.html), [provided an empty connection string is supplied](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/libpq-connect.html#LIBPQ-PQCONNECTDB).

This problem exists in all versions of SQLAlchemy including 1.3.2 (the latest as of writing):

Explicit passing of connection parameters in connection URL:

```
$ python
Python 3.6.5 (default, Mar 29 2018, 15:37:32)
[GCC 4.2.1 Compatible Apple LLVM 9.0.0 (clang-900.0.39.2)] on darwin
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import sqlalchemy
>>> sqlalchemy.__version__
'1.3.2'
>>> from sqlalchemy import create_engine
>>> engine = create_engine('postgresql://localhost/sqlalchemy-test')
>>> conn = engine.connect()
>>> result = conn.execute('SELECT 42')
>>> result.scalar()
42
```

Connection URL without connection parameters but with `PGHOST` and `PGDATABASE` env vars specified:

```
$ PGHOST=localhost PGDATABASE=sqlalchemy-test python
```

OK it seems like if you send *any* parameters to psycopg2, even connect_timeout, then you dont need "dsn".   this is an odd design but im going to ask on #4562 about this also.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Propagate query-arg-only URL to psycopg2; don't send blank host** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1185
